answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before receiving one scarce work permit. Accepted work raises its beacon score, while random yarrow audits check claims and a permit fee consumes a relic resource. A fake identity must therefore immobilize the full bond and pay the fee before competing; multiplying identities multiplies this upfront cost, making a Sybil farm expensive rather than free.
